tags.effort_rationale: Expanded to 49 official industries and the market, five SEC-filed thematic ETF proxies, and an incremental source sync with bounded range re-sync controls and user documentation.

objective: Expand the responsive U.S. industry seasonality explorer to 49 official industry portfolios plus the market benchmark, add clearly sourced short-history thematic ETF/index proxies, include the latest available 2026 months, and publish through the GitHub Pages homepage. Add an on-demand incremental sync command for new/missing months and ranged re-syncs.

evidence: 2026-11-01: Rebuilt the 49-industry panel from the official September 2026 archive (SHA-256 d1a3b0b9896e1e633ed2aa85e24ca144d7998f8ab2ff344e2379383ebeb7b836) plus the official monthly factor archive (SHA-256 b03d39e4bb253dda0f14893db3b78e64b40b8d6549a0fc0fd4111dae84c98618). Verified 369 contiguous month rows (1996-01 through 2026-09), 49 industry columns plus market, complete historical months and Mkt-RF + RF arithmetic. October is not present in the current official release.
2026-11-01: Rebuilt from the pinned official ZIP files and compared byte-for-byte with the committed source dataset; output matched exactly.
2026-11-01: Dynamic parser fixture extended the source archive beyond the pinned September 2026 endpoint and verified October ingestion and market return aggregation.

2026-10-31: npm run build (frontend/): Vite production build passed. Local browser inspection confirmed the /seasonality navigation item, all-years default and 30 year labels. Slider moved to 2025 and changed the page to the 2025 monthly rows and one chart line; selecting Beer & liquor updated the selected chart. Desktop screenshot showed all 12 months. Mobile-width screenshot review remains pending.
2026-11-01: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund succeeded; npm run build passed with Vite 5.4.21 after the market series and search behavior were added.
2026-11-01: Standard and Pages builds passed after expanding to the official 49-industry panel and adding the partial 2026 selector.
2026-11-01: Rebuilt the standard Vite app after adding the five SEC-backed proxies; production build passed (one existing chunk-size advisory, no build errors).

checks.description: Review desktop navigation, all-years/default and year-specific states, row selection, chart values and source/method labels.
evidence: 2026-10-31: Local browser inspection covered navigation, all-years heatmap, slider 2025 state, industry selection, 30/1 chart series and source/method labels. Desktop screenshot showed all 12 month columns.

checks.description: Inspect page and navigation at phone viewport widths, including full heatmap month values and chart usability.
evidence: 2026-11-01: At 390×844 the heatmap used its contained horizontal scroller and chart stayed within viewport; the full set of 55 rows remained available without page-level horizontal overflow.

checks.description: Verify clicking a chart year fades other years, clicking it again restores all years, and month points expose the return and comparison metrics.
evidence: 2026-11-01: All-years chart rendered one line per available year and keyboard-focusable month points expose return and monthly-average comparison. The existing year legend buttons toggle focus and restore all lines; the same interaction was inspected after the current 49+market+proxy integration.

checks.description: Use authoritative, reusable market total-return time series for AI, robotics, quantum, nuclear, and renewable proxies; preserve each proxy definition, source, start date, period, and data rights.
evidence: 2026-11-01: Added AIQ, ROBO, QTUM, NLR, and ICLN as explicitly labeled theme proxies using SEC EDGAR Form N-PORT Item B.5 fund-reported class total returns. Each series has its own start/end dates and links exact filings, accession IDs, reported fields/values, and source hashes; no inferred or Yahoo data is used. Issuer pages identify fund strategy; these are not uniform official industry classifications.

checks.description: Include verified 2026 industry and market months through October, with later months absent and clearly labeled.
evidence: 2026-11-01: Official French industry and market histories are available through September 2026; SEC proxy histories end between June and August 2026. All October cells are blank because none of the checked public source records contains October return observations.

checks.description: Human reviews the full diff and decides whether to accept the feature before commit or publication.

evidence: 2026-11-01: scripts/planning/validate_ticket.py accepted the manifest and all 22 changed ticket paths. The stock-research guide is an explicit exact-file exception; unrelated schedule/skill and draft-ticket changes remain outside scope.
2026-11-01: npm run build -- --mode pages succeeded and produced the standalone GitHub Pages app under artifacts/seasonality with the configured project asset path.

checks.description: Inspect the homepage tile and static seasonality page, select the market series, and verify the all-years chart.
evidence: 2026-11-01: Local browser inspection of /seasonality showed the all-years default, 49 industries + market + five sourced proxies, 12 monthly cells, official 369-month range and the selected-series chart. AI, robotics, quantum, nuclear and renewable rows display ETF tickers and their actual SEC coverage windows.

checks.description: After required human review and push, verify the Pages workflow succeeded and the public homepage tile and seasonality section load.

evidence: 2026-11-01: Two deterministic SEC extraction tests passed. Verified N-PORT rtn1/rtn2/rtn3 align to report month minus two/month minus one/report month, class/series validation, contiguous filing-linked monthly histories, exact SEC filing URLs, accession IDs, and SHA-256 metadata for AIQ (2019-09–2026-08), ROBO (2019-08–2026-07), QTUM (2020-01–2026-06), NLR (2019-07–2026-06), and ICLN (2019-07–2026-07).
2026-11-01: Incremental-fetch regression test confirms existing SEC accessions do not trigger filing XML downloads.

2026-11-01: Five deterministic sync tests passed for conditional HTTP 304 behavior, month filtering, default missing-only merges, range overwrite versus --missing-only, and calendar-month argument validation. A live source run against temporary JSON copies verified both official French archive downloads, SEC known-accession skips, no new values at the current source as-of date, and repeat-run HTTP 304 responses with no archive payload.

acceptance.description: Reproducibly extract the official 49 value-weighted industry portfolio series and market benchmark for 1996-01 through the latest available month, with provenance.
evidence: Rebuilt and validated 369 contiguous official monthly observations across 49 industries through September 2026; source archives are pinned by SHA-256.

acceptance.description: Reach the page through Praesagus navigation and inspect all-years aggregation and all year selections.
evidence: Production build passed; local browser showed the navigation route and default all-years heatmap. Slider moved to 2025 and displayed the single-year observations and chart.

acceptance.description: Select an industry row and verify year-specific and all-years chart series.
evidence: Local browser selection changed the industry heading/series; all-years chart exposed 30 year labels and the 2025 chart one year label.

acceptance.description: Show source, method, units, uncertainty and illustrative company examples accurately.
evidence: Inspected page copy for Fama/French source, SIC industries, total return method, monthly percent values, 1996–2025 mean, revision caveat, illustrative example limitation and no-signal disclaimer.

acceptance.description: Extract and align the official market benchmark as Mkt-RF + RF; expose it as an interactive table row and chart series.
evidence: The pinned Fama/French monthly factor archive parsed to 360 complete market returns aligned by YYYYMM; exact endpoint values and Mkt-RF + RF arithmetic passed focused tests. Local interaction changed selection to Overall U.S. market and rendered 30 annual chart lines.

acceptance.description: Create a Pages-mode standalone build and direct homepage tile, and include both in the existing Pages workflow.
evidence: The Pages-mode static bundle was generated in artifacts/seasonality with project-path asset URLs. The homepage tile linked directly to it in a local static Pages-path preview. The public Pages workflow has not run yet.

acceptance.description: Verify responsive layout and focused tests/builds in frontend and GitHub Pages modes.
evidence: Focused dataset and SEC proxy tests pass; standard and Pages Vite builds pass; local responsive and interaction review recorded.

acceptance.description: Select a chart year to emphasize it and fade the rest, toggle it off by selecting it again, and inspect monthly point return statistics.
evidence: Local Pages preview verified focused and restored chart states and exact monthly return, 30-year average, and percentage-point difference in each point label/title.

acceptance.description: Add official semiconductor and software industry series plus AI, robotics, quantum, nuclear, and renewable theme proxies, each with explicit source, method and coverage dates.
evidence: The French 49-industry series includes official Chips/Semiconductors and Softw/Software portfolios. AI, robotics, quantum, nuclear and renewable rows use the five source-linked SEC filing series described by the thematic-sources check.
Automated SEC proxy test validates the five source-linked series and exact coverage windows.

acceptance.description: Show official and proxy 2026 observations only through each source’s latest verified month; leave October onward blank until published by the source.
evidence: Industry/market data ends September 2026; SEC fund proxies end June–August 2026. October is unavailable in all selected sources as of the retrieval date.

acceptance.description: Complete independent human scope/visual review, then verify the public Pages deployment before accepting delivery.

Provide an on-demand seasonality sync for market, industry and five theme series; default to new missing months, support a selected month and start-year/rolling-year re-sync with missing-only behavior, retain source provenance, and document use beside the stock-research CSV generation guide.
evidence: The new sync command uses conditional HTTP requests for the two French monthly archives, skips already captured SEC filing XML by accession, filters one-month or range operations, and merges only the chosen missing/re-sync window. The stock-research README explains commands, cadence, source limitations and the separation from prediction CSV generation.
